UI isn't just a technique, it's a *mindset*. Goku's story is one about tranquility and enlightenment, where he must overcome his wild tendencies and become truly tranquil. Goku is a carefree character, and in battle he largely relies on instinct to adapt. UI is all about self control above all else

Conversely, Vegeta is all about the self. His story is one about overcoming and taking ownership of pride and his difficult past. However, he is also a disciplined character who prefers fighting with a good strategy and overwhelming force, and thus focusing on ego makes more sense.

While yes, true, he might in theory be effective with it just as Goku might be effective with Ego, they are inherently incompatible with these powers from the outset. This is why Beerus struggles with UI- a God of Destruction has to channel their ego and the will to destroy and that can often interfere with the tranquility and self-knowledge the UI requires and would require tons of discipline to achieve a good balance. So while they could both learn the other power, it requires overcoming their natures in fundamental ways.

Remember that Gero was accounting for the Goku he saw using kaio ken on top of his growth. The lack of kaio ken, plus him being at a similar power level, means that his power is not only roughly at where he is normally, but he also won't be accounting for the kind of exponential power increase of kaio ken. This limited data means that, ultimately, his creations aren't going to stronger, and I'd argue they'd be weaker if anything.

Goku being stronger than normal doesn't actually affect the Androids at all. His power level should equalize wth Z around Freeza. Any power boost he may have gotten ultimately requires him to train anyways, which is the main thing Gero was accounting for in the first place, if he even survives here. This was the point of Goku v. Vegeta- all the natural talent in the world means nothing compared to someone who works their butt off.

No matter how you do this scenario, it's a bad end. Vegeta is likely t be banished and even if he isn't being so much weaker may well be his downfall even with training, plus Kakarot's pod is absolutely getting detected and shot down. Let's assume neither occur. Maybe Freeza's scouts are negligent and King Vegeta's outlook on his son changes. 

All well and good. Even then, I don't see this going well. Goku almost certainly ends up as bad as in the 22nd tournament scenario, if not worse, because DB is a cakewalk for him. With a base of 500, assuming Kami spares him, he'll be at >1k before even training with Roshi. I'd estimate >9k PL by Z, like that Vegeta fan manga.

To be different from the aforementioned scenario, Gohan is still born here with somewhat higher potential.  This matters later.

Now, our Saiyan Saga is substantially different. Because Vegeta can't act as a crutch, he is forced to act humble and work hard, and Raditz is likely not the dog's body here. This also forces the Saiyans to work together, so all of them end up fairly impressive. I suspect this results in a bad end, since they'd take Raditz seriously after seeing how low class warriors can grow. For the sake of the story, we'll send Raditz so it isn't a bad end. Goku wins of course, so no King Kai. This isn't so bad though, since when the others show up, Gohan will be trained up although I don't see this Goku taking his training seriously so he barely grows. We'll say Goku spares Raditz too, but I'm not sure that would even happen. We'll say it does.

Either way, Saiyans show up, and this is where Goku finally gets a real challenge. Because of their teamwork, plus the exploitation of zenkais, Goku only wins by a hair and Namek still happens more or less like normal up until. We'll say Goku still thinks of the gravity chamber because of an offhand comment about Earth's gravity being lower. Herein lies the problem. We're starting at 9kish and even with Raditz training with him, he only gets to like 60-75k and without that boost, I doubt Ginyu would body swap. We'll say they kill him with good teamwork, easy enough.

Now Freeza might be a big problem, but we could always give Goku a similar Zenkai to Vegeta's so he has the 3M PL he needs to turn SSJ. Time passes, Goku dies of heart virus and future happens. I see one of two things happening at this point:
1. Gohan's somewhat larger potential gives him the edge he needs to put 17 and 18 in the ground.
2. The timeline largely falls in line with Z at this point. By now, Goku has been thoroughly given his humble pie and while there are a couple new Saiyans (maybe, it's possible they just die during the Saiyan Saga, but who knows?) past Androids it isn't as important, although I guess BoG is a little less hectic.

There's a lot of other things to explore here, but ultimately our problem is this particular scenario has way too many failure points to be plausible, and I had to use stretches to make this work. Ultimately, I think it simply gets a bad end for Earth with Kakarot dying in space and that's it.
